items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I think she's the only one Bessie Smith ever complained about, you see, because she sang some song -- I think it was 'Syria' or something she sang, and Bessie Smith used to sing the same song.

ctx.x: Yeah, it was a review, see. She used to have a review. The Brown Skin Buddies was a review, but it was like the -- Chinch and Ella B. Moore Revies -- Brown Skin Buddies, see? They were -- they were like what you call stars, you see. And she was from Texas, this lady. She was from Dallas, Texas. And she had a theater there. It was called the Beaulah Theater, and she -- she sold it to some white people, and they changed the name of it -- the theater to the Dallas Theater, you see.

And because she used to travel, you know, in the South, and she was a great singer, beautiful voice, very good singing. I think she's the only one Bessie Smith ever complained about, you see, because she sang some song -- I think it was 'Syria' or something she sang, and Bessie Smith used to sing the same song. But -- no disrespect, but I think Ella B. Moore had a prettier voice than Bessie Smith, you see.

But, see, she used to calk up. She used to blackface. She was a woman, a female blackface comedian, because that's what he was, Chinch Moore, you see. I say they were of course stars. It was their show, because they had had the Brown Skin Models, number one. Then they had Brown Skin Models number two, and then they had Brown Skin Buddies, and that was the last of the shows. Then they was going to stop doing the shows, you see.
